look_here_first: Start with the leaves. Forestiera pubescens has noticeably broader elliptic to ovate leaves with some pubescence, and it is winter-deciduous. The rigid paired side branches still make the classic 'elbow' architecture.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: subopposite to opposite branch pattern with rigid paired lateral branches

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves elliptic to broadly lanceolate/ovate or obovate, much broader than F. angustifolia

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf surfaces often with scattered short hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers appear before leaves and lack a corolla

lookalikes.differences: F. angustifolia has very narrow linear leathery leaves, often clustered on twigs, and is evergreen to semi-evergreen/drought-deciduous rather than winter-deciduous.
